column1: # Column -> struct offset for every runtime table, from the 56 DB_Bind__<TABLE>
# binders. Each binding is a name, then TWO integers, then a std::map lookup:
# WHICH OF THE TWO IS THE OFFSET IS NOT FIXED BY SOURCE ORDER. Round 308 assumed
# it was the first and got 18 of 409 wrong; round 309 assumed the more DISTINCT
# one, which is right for _CHAR but wrong for _SiegeFortress, where the other
# variable is a dense column INDEX (0,2,3,4..10) and equally distinct.
# The discriminator that works: an offset is distinct AND sparse. A column index
# is a near-consecutive run, so its density (distinct / (max-min+1)) approaches 1;
# a struct offset's is far lower (_CHAR: 43 columns over 0x20..0xf2, density 0.20).
# CONTROLS, all exact: _CHAR Strength 0x74, RemainHwanCount 0x86 (both recovered
# independently by earlier rounds), PosX/PosY/PosZ 0x98/0x9c/0xa0, and
# _SiegeFortress FortressID 0x18 / Introduction 0x38 -- the last two added because
# the _CHAR controls alone passed while the parse was wrong.
# STRUCTURAL: no (table, offset) pair repeats in the 409.
# INDEPENDENTLY RE-DERIVED (round 310): the same offsets were extracted a second time
# from raw DISASSEMBLY -- per binding the compiler emits `mov DWORD PTR [esp+A], <offset>`
# then `mov DWORD PTR [esp+B], <code>` then `call 0x862e40`, and slot A is fixed for a
# whole function. That path shares no failure mode with the decompiler read (no STL
# reconstruction, no variable naming, no source-order assumption). All 50 tables it
# covers are IDENTICAL, 403 offsets. The other 6 are the single-column binders, which
# have too few bindings to identify a slot and are settled by sibling agreement instead.
# The six `Slot` rows come from single-column binders, where there is no
# distribution to test. They are resolved instead by agreement: all six sibling
# container tables bind Slot at 0x18 with code 2, in six separate functions.
# `code` is RECORDED, NOT INTERPRETED. It is not a width -- it differs from the
# next-offset delta in 332 of 353 cases. No use-site has been read.
